title: Background Data for: Impact of Latency on Task Performance and User Experience in Teleoperated Object Manipulation
rights: CC BY 4.0 per Zenodo and readme. Credit Myrthe E. J. Tilleman, Konstantinos Kousias, Ozgu Alay, Carsten Griwodz and Jim Torresen. Derived tables contain only aggregated outcome counts and paired changes.

keys: Background Data for: Impact of Latency on Task Performance and User Experience in Teleoperated Object Manipulation
Impact of Latency on Task Performance and User Experience in Teleoperated Object Manipulation

related_paper.evidence: Data release and methods README read; final article was not verified as free full text.

physical_task: Co-located UR10e and Shadow hand driven by a tracked glove, immediate visual feedback of real arm. Five command execution conditions (0,50,100,150,200 ms) were programmed. The release has per-completed-task outcomes, how many restarts occurred, and questionnaires. It does not have physical per-command actuation timestamps, independent end-to-end delay measurements, failed-trial durations or trajectories.
coverage: Study planned 49 people; one calibration abort generated no rows. All 480 released rows over 48 distinct people checked. One person had repeated baseline in JTHFT and no 150-ms entry. Paper exclusion set from README leaves 450 rows and 45 people. Across all rows 139 restarts occur over 100 eventual completions; all reason counts can be reconciled (68 hardware,69 participant,2 other).
method: Separate JTHFT successful completion time in seconds from BBT block count in a fixed minute. Compute changes within person relative to 0 ms and require exactly one row for each member of a pair. Run once on all recorded data, then repeat after the authors’ four stated exclusions (2,7,10,32; no rows from 32). Outcomes are conditioned on successful completion; counts of restarts are kept. No participant-level values are published here.
findings: Using 45 paper-analysis participants, 200 ms vs baseline has median within-person change +12.85207 s in JTHFT (37 slower, 8 faster), and −2 blocks/min in BBT (35 lower,7 same,3 higher). The BBT median change at 50 and 100 ms is 0 blocks/min. Hardware disruptions and repeats prevent inference about all-attempt completion times.
reproduce: python derive_oslo.py latency_teleoperation_user_study_data.tsv OUT (Python 3 plus NumPy).
